Wadi Ghadir · Eastern Desert, Egypt · SimPEG 0.25

Wadi Ghadir SimPEG Inversions

Three Jupyter notebooks invert the Wadi Ghadir survey in 3-D on one common mesh below the Copernicus topography: the complete Bouguer anomaly for density, the total-field magnetic anomaly for susceptibility, and both together, coupled by a cross-gradient term so that the two models share their structure.

Written by Mohamed Sobh, LIAG · Leibniz Institute for Applied Geophysics, Hannover

Density from gravity

Dense rock (red) follows a NE–SW belt through the centre of the survey; light material (blue) fills the south-western corner and the north-east. The model reaches about ±0.1 g/cm³ relative to 2.67 g/cm³.

Susceptibility from magnetics

The strongest magnetic sources lie in the south-west and in the centre (about 691 km E, 2742 km N), up to 0.12 SI. Where an induced body sits below the ground, the reduced-to-pole map of the magnetic chain shows its high.

Joint inversion

The joint models fit both data sets as well as the separate ones, but their boundaries now coincide: the gradient-weighted structural dissimilarity falls from 0.33 to 0.044 (87 % lower). Values are not tied together: a dense body may be magnetic or not.

Choosing the coupling weight λ

Test runs of the joint inversion (25 iterations each). λ = 10⁹ is the strongest coupling that still fits both data sets.

λgravity rms [mGal]magnetic rms [nT]both fitted
0 (uncoupled)0.1146yes
10⁸0.1145yes
10⁹0.0943yes
3·10⁹0.1675no
10¹⁰0.2594no

Reading the models

Potential-field data do not determine a unique model. Each inversion returns the smallest and smoothest sensitivity-weighted model that fits the data to their uncertainties; depths and shapes depend on these choices.

The magnetic models assume induced magnetisation along today's field (IGRF-14, survey date assumed 20 January 2026); remanence would move or reshape the bodies. Cells far from the data are unconstrained and are blanked in the slices.

Mesh: 400 m × 400 m × 100 m core cells, 81 × 57 × 28 cells, 105,895 below the Copernicus GLO-30 topography. Models are exported as NumPy and UBC-GIF files in outputs/inversion/; shared code in wghadir/inversion.py.
